strands.name: Cognitive offloading: the frame
strands.note: The core theory the paper works with. Offloading is defined as the use of external resources to lower cognitive demand (Risko and Gilbert, 2015), given a metacognitive account (Dunn and Risko, 2016), shown to be strategic when a future need is expected (Gilbert, 2015), and measured as a trade: immediate performance rises while memory for the offloaded content falls (Grinschgl et al., 2021).

strands.name: Working memory and subjective confidence
strands.note: The cognitive-psychology roots: the limits of working memory (Baddeley, 2012) and the confidence judgement that decides when a person stops thinking and starts delegating (Koriat, 2012).

strands.name: Distributed cognition and the reflective practitioner
strands.note: The older education and human-computer interaction roots: cognition distributed across people and tools (Hollan et al., 2000), reflection in action (Schon, 2017), and Shulman's (1986, 1987) account of teacher knowledge and reasoning, which is the bridge from cognition to teaching.

strands.name: Teacher data use, judgement and learning analytics
strands.note: The neighbouring literature that supplies the teacher-as-regulator vocabulary: data-based decision-making (Datnow, 2016; Mandinach, 2016; Schildkamp, 2019; Vanlommel, 2019) and the learning-analytics and dashboard work (Ifenthaler, 2020; Schwendimann, 2016; Verbert, 2014; Viberg, 2018).

strands.name: Generative AI in teaching: a young review literature
strands.note: The field the study positions itself against. Mostly systematic reviews of GenAI in education, with 2025 the heaviest year (Chiu, 2024; Holmes, 2019; Samala, 2025; Wang, 2025; Wanyonyi, 2025; Tan, 2025; Xia, 2026; Zhang, 2025, and others). The median reference year of the whole list is 2023, which shows how quickly this literature has grown.

strands.name: Ethics, disclosure and AI literacy: the normative debate
strands.note: The controversy the paper enters: ethical leadership in the AI era (Ho, 2025), teachers' ethical awareness (Ho, 2025), disclosure statements in teaching (Overono, 2025) and a critical review of social-emotional learning with GenAI (Henriksen, 2025).

strands.name: Method: qualitative research
strands.note: The method sources: thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke, 2006), interview research (Kvale, 2009), qualitative research practice (Patton, 2015), participant selection (Severiano, 2025) and case study design (Yin, 2018). A qualitative design is still unusual in this review-heavy field.

strands.note: Crossref gave neither an author nor a title for these entries. They are listed exactly as they arrived, and no attempt was made to complete them from memory.

doi_10.1016_j.caeai.2026.100670.narrative:
The frame comes from the cognitive-offloading line. Risko and Gilbert (2015, 2016) define offloading as the use of external resources to reduce cognitive demand, Dunn and Risko (2016) give it a metacognitive account, and Gilbert (2015) shows that people offload strategically when they expect a future need for the material. Grinschgl et al. (2021) supply the warning that runs through the study: offloading lifts immediate performance while lowering later memory for the content that was delegated. Two older traditions sit underneath, the working-memory and confidence research (Baddeley, 2012; Koriat, 2012) and the education and human-computer interaction roots in distributed cognition and reflective practice (Hollan et al., 2000; Schon, 2017), with Shulman's (1986, 1987) account of teacher knowledge as the bridge to teachers.

The rest of the list is the context the study argues with. Much of it is the fast-growing GenAI-in-education review literature (Chiu, 2024; Samala, 2025; Wang, 2025; Wanyonyi, 2025; Xia, 2026), next to the teacher data-use and learning-analytics work (Schildkamp, 2019; Vanlommel, 2019; Verbert, 2014; Viberg, 2018) and a normative strand on ethics, disclosure and AI literacy (Ho, 2025; Overono, 2025; Henriksen, 2025). The median reference year is 2023 and the earliest is 1986, so the list is young with a thin older spine. The method sources (Braun and Clarke, 2006; Kvale, 2009; Patton, 2015) mark the paper's own approach: a qualitative study in a field that mostly reviews itself.
doi_10.1016_j.caeai.2026.100670.forYou: This is the literature base under your Professional Criticality argument. The offloading frame gives you the mechanism, the data-use and analytics work gives you the teacher context, and the review layer shows how crowded the space around you already is.
doi_10.1016_j.caeai.2026.100670.absent: Nothing is written from outside the English-language literature, and there is no source on epistemic justice or decolonial critique of AI, although your own corpus now holds one (Berman and Smithies, 2026). No workplace or Dutch source appears either, so the transfer to a hogeschool setting is untested by this list.
